why: The earlier source checkout was not the current release and the private client runtime is not a public SDK
result: pin ready for executable verification

decision: Requested designated Slack workspace channel and tester IDs without asking for secrets in chat
why: Live tests need explicit authority and credentials must stay out of transcripts
result: workspace identified; app channel and testers still pending

decision: Chose a SQLite command log with stateless workers and per-task leases
why: It makes crash recovery queryable without adding an event bus or long-lived actor state
result: design settled; two external candidates dropped at platform usage limit

decision: Minted a T3 token restricted to orchestration read and operate scopes
why: The setup token has administrative authority and must never run the service
result: real server accepted exact scopes and denied the administrative clients endpoint with HTTP 403

decision: Completed an Effect RPC probe against the official T3 0.0.42 binary
why: The private client runtime cannot be assumed compatible without an executable handshake
result: real server probe and config decode succeeded; six provider entries found

decision: Kept the handwritten T3 wire adapter behind parsed domain values
why: The upstream contracts and client runtime are private workspace packages, while the release server exposes a stable authenticated boundary
result: live probe, exact-scope denial, provider catalog, and command replay tests passed

decision: Separated tool-free provider completion from supervised command approval
why: A provider turn and an approval boundary are different behaviors and need independent evidence
result: real Codex turn completed; one-shot command approvals resolved and completed a second turn

decision: Stopped using raw T3 runtime logs for diagnostics
why: Headless startup output contains a bootstrap code even though the consumed code reports authenticated false
result: future diagnostics use parsed snapshots or whitelisted database fields; no active credential entered evidence

decision: Made SQLite transactions the inbox operation lease and outbox commit boundary
why: Stable IDs and recoverable leases prevent Slack retries or process exits from creating blind T3 and Slack replays
result: deduplication reopen lease expiry ordering concurrency outbox and injected rollback fixtures passed

decision: Used channel and message timestamp as the canonical inbound event key
why: Slack retries and overlapping app mention and message subscriptions can have different delivery IDs for one human message
result: overlap collapsed to one durable operation; authorized threaded steering preserved identity and order

decision: Quarantined expired Slack sends instead of automatically replaying them
why: The supported chat.postMessage surface has no documented idempotency key and Slack says some errors may follow partial success
result: ambiguous sends become operator-visible failures without a blind duplicate write

decision: Made the coordinator a durable T3 command mapper rather than an agent runtime
why: T3 must remain the only execution backend while Agent Tag owns leases identity routing and Slack delivery
result: a real stored operation completed in a managed T3 worktree and atomically produced its Slack outbox reply

decision: Persisted provider requests and human responses before T3 dispatch
why: Slack acknowledgements process exits retries and stale clicks must not lose or duplicate an approval question or cancellation
result: restart fixtures passed; real T3 accept decline and interrupt controls passed

decision: Ran bounded stateless workers under one foreground lifecycle
why: Coordinator interaction and Slack delivery need independent progress and one recoverable shutdown boundary
result: fixture lifecycle and log canary passed; real T3 operation reconciled after store and worker restart

decision: Made backup restore non-destructive and audit export content-minimal
why: Operational recovery must not overwrite a live store or leak Slack message bodies
result: integrity-checked private backup restored to a new path; existing destination rejected; audit rows excluded message text

decision: Required startup catalog validation plus real execution evidence
why: A T3 provider can report ready and authenticated while its runtime API calls still fail
result: Codex real turn passed; Claude Opus default and Sonnet selections all failed with provider-api-errors; T3-04 marked FAIL

decision: Kept memory scoped attributed expiring and explicitly untrusted in provider prompts
why: Team context must not cross profile task or private identity boundaries or mutate an idempotent replay
result: four-scope access and denial fixtures passed; rendered turn text stayed immutable across retry

decision: Derived every scheduled run identity from schedule and due time
why: A crash after inbox or outbox insertion must replay the same semantic run while missed and overlapping work follow explicit policy
result: restart fake-clock reminder cancellation missed-run and overlap fixtures passed

decision: Made ambient participation profile opt-in and fingerprint-bounded
why: An unmentioned channel message must not silently spend provider work or repeatedly react to unchanged content
result: default-off relevance unchanged cooldown and hourly-cap fixtures passed with durable audits

decision: Added streamed exact-canary and known-pattern scans that never return matched values
why: Release evidence needs a repeatable repository data prompt and artifact leak check rather than manual inspection
result: binary boundary canary fixture passed; 64-file repository scan found no credentials and skipped no symlinks

decision: Required lease recovery to survive SIGKILL without cleanup
why: Close-and-reopen and transaction faults do not prove behavior after actual process death
result: fresh process respected live lease then recovered stable operation command and message IDs at attempt two

decision: Bound every DM route and durable task to one allowed human
why: A generic allowed-user check can leak private context when several humans share a workspace profile
result: config router store memory coordinator and schedule boundaries enforce durable DM ownership; live Slack exercise remains
